Let’s dive into Chapter 7: Managing Teams—Trust, Autonomy, and the Value of Small Groups.
As a business grows, managing people gets trickier, doesn’t it? Traditional management often leans on layers of hierarchy, strict rules, and constant oversight. But here’s the thing—the best teams thrive on trust, autonomy, and clear communication.
Picture a jazz band. Each musician brings their own flair, improvising within a shared rhythm. There’s no one standing over them, dictating every note. Instead, it’s trust and mutual respect that let them create something amazing together.
In business, it works the same way. Small, empowered teams can pull off incredible results when they’re trusted to make decisions and truly own their work.
Here’s what happens with micromanagement: it crushes initiative and slows everything down. Instead, leaders should focus on setting clear goals, offering support, and then... stepping back. Sure, mistakes will happen—they always do. But those missteps? They’re also some of the best opportunities to learn and grow.
So, what’s the recipe for managing a great team? Let’s break it down:
First— keep teams small. Fewer people means everybody’s on the same page, and decisions come faster.
Second— trust your team. Give folks the freedom to do their thing, and hold them responsible for what they deliver.
Third— minimize the rules. Instead of rigid policies, rely on common sense and shared values.
And finally— encourage open feedback. Build a culture where anyone can speak up, share ideas, or voice concerns without fear.
Think about a software startup. They might split into small, cross-functional teams, with each group owning a specific feature or project. They get to pick how they work and set their own timelines. That kind of structure sparks innovation, builds accountability, and gives everyone a real sense of ownership.
So, when businesses build teams around trust and autonomy, they unlock creativity and resilience. It’s how you stay nimble, adapt to new challenges, and seize new opportunities as they come.
